title: shadow traffic: emit shadow_eval events + sampling metadata; link primary<->shadow via request_id
author: Caleb Johnson
body: Summary: This PR adds first-pass telemetry emission for Shadow Traffic evaluations. For any request that is sampled into shadow execution, we emit normalized shadow_eval events to the telemetry pipeline and attach sampling + routing metadata needed to compare candidate targets against the primary response. The design goal is to make analysis possible without requiring raw prompt/response storage by default, while still enabling request-level joins (primary<->shadow) for debugging and judge scoring. Details: (1) Request ID linking: we propagate the existing request_id from the primary request into the shadow job payload and telemetry, and we generate a shadow_request_id for each shadow target execution. The pair (request_id, shadow_request_id) uniquely identifies a shadow run. We also emit a stable eval_run_id (UUID) to group all shadow targets for a single sampled primary request. (2) Sampling metadata: when policy evaluation decides to shadow, we emit fields like shadow.sampled=true, shadow.sample_rate (0-1), shadow.policy_id, shadow.policy_version, shadow.decision_reason (bucketed), and shadow.target_id / shadow.target_kind (model|config|quant_profile). We deliberately avoid putting customer-provided route names or arbitrary user tags in event dimensions; we only include route_id (stable internal ID) and a low-cardinality route_group (optional). (3) Event types: we emit shadow_eval.request_mirrored (at mirror decision time), shadow_eval.shadow_enqueued (when job is accepted), shadow_eval.shadow_started, shadow_eval.shadow_completed (includes token counts, model identifier, outcome), and shadow_eval.shadow_failed (error_class is normalized + bucketed). These are emitted as structured events into telemetry-events (Kafka) and are also recorded as OTEL span attributes on the shadow execution span for trace correlation. (4) Performance/cost fields: for completed runs we emit latency_ms (total, queue_wait, model_exec), prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, and compute_estimated_usd (derived using the same metering model as primary). These are used for deltas and gating thresholds. (5) Redaction posture: this PR intentionally does not ship raw prompt/response capture. It only emits lengths/token counts and hashed identifiers where needed (e.g., prompt_hash for optional join with restricted payload logging in a separate PR). A follow-up PR will wire optional payload sampling behind restricted logging + retention controls. Example event (shape only, values illustrative): {"event":"shadow_eval.shadow_completed","request_id":"req_01J...","shadow_request_id":"shreq_01J...","eval_run_id":"eval_01J...","route_id":"rt_7f2c...","region":"us-east-1","shadow":{"sampled":true,"sample_rate":0.05,"policy_id":"pol_3c1d...","policy_version":"14","decision_reason":"allowlist"},"target":{"id":"tgt_9a0b...","kind":"model","model":"llama-3.1-70b-instruct","model_revision":"2025-10-18"},"perf":{"latency_ms":812,"queue_wait_ms":34,"model_exec_ms":742},"usage":{"prompt_tokens":521,"completion_tokens":146,"total_tokens":667},"cost":{"compute_estimated_usd":0.0069},"outcome":"ok"}. Testing: unit tests for schema validation + normalization; integration test that shadow jobs emit the expected event sequence and that request_id/shadow_request_id are present on both telemetry event and trace span. Rollout: safe behind shadow traffic feature flag (no effect if shadowing disabled). Notes: This PR does not define aggregation tables/dashboards; it focuses on emitting the canonical event stream with low-cardinality tags. Checklist: [x] event names follow shadow_eval.* naming; [x] dimensions reviewed for cardinality; [x] request_id propagation verified end-to-end; [x] schema compatibility check in CI; [x] docs comment added for internal consumers.
commits: telemetry(shadow): add shadow_eval event definitions + JSON schema
shadow-runner: propagate request_id and generate shadow_request_id/eval_run_id
telemetry: emit shadow_eval.request_mirrored and enqueue/start/complete/failed events
otel: attach shadow metadata to shadow execution span attributes
tests: add schema normalization + integration coverage
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Please ensure event names match the shadow_eval.* standard and that tag keys are lower_snake_case. Also, confirm we do not emit raw route names as dimensions.

Caleb Johnson (author): Updated event names to shadow_eval.request_mirrored/shadow_enqueued/shadow_started/shadow_completed/shadow_failed and renamed shadow.sampleRate -> shadow.sample_rate. Route name removed; only route_id + optional route_group (bucketed) remain.

Thomas Baird (review): Cardinality risk: target.id and policy_id look unbounded. Are these stable IDs with manageable cardinality? Also error_class needs bucketing; please avoid sending raw exception messages.

Caleb Johnson (author): target.id/policy_id are internal stable IDs and we expect low-ish cardinality per account, but to be safe I added tag_bucketing: decision_reason is allowlisted; error_class is mapped to a small enum; removed exception.message and stack; added guard that any unknown error maps to "unknown".

Nadia Rahman (review): For cost attribution, compute_estimated_usd should use the same metering model as primary, otherwise deltas will be misleading. Do we have model_revision in the payload for rate selection?

Caleb Johnson (author): Yes—wired through metering/rates by (model, model_revision, region, quant_profile). Added model_revision to target and included quant_profile when present. cost.compute_estimated_usd now calls the shared usage estimator.

Mei Lin (review): Analytics needs a reliable join key. request_id is ok, but please add eval_run_id to group multiple shadow targets for the same primary sampled request. Also ensure timestamps are consistent (ms since epoch).

Caleb Johnson (author): Added eval_run_id (UUID) generated at mirror decision time and carried through each target execution. Timestamps are emitted as event_time_ms (epoch millis) with server clock; validated in tests.

Logan Wright (review): Looks good. One request: emit shadow_eval.shadow_enqueued only after the job is accepted (i.e., capacity check passes). If we emit before enqueue and then drop, it complicates drop-rate computation.

Caleb Johnson (author): Good catch—moved shadow_enqueued emission to after enqueue acknowledgement, and added shadow_eval.shadow_failed with outcome="dropped" and error_class="capacity_budget" for drops. Added integration test that drop paths produce a single failure event.
Thomas Baird (review): Approved after bucketing changes.
